note: Both sets capture the text-stated gains (KP(θ=0°)=0.01882681 s, KI(θ=0°)=0.008068634, KD=0.0 s²) and the damping ratio ζφ = 0.7, and both read Figure 7-4 in essentially the same way. Set B repeats the erroneous 0.020 s proportional-gain-at-0° claim twice and gives 0.005 s at 25° where A gives 0.004 s, so B carries one extra wrong/duplicate claim; otherwise the two sets are near-identical. Both invent values at 25° even though the plotted curves end near 23°, both restate the θ=0 gains with off plot-read values (0.020 s, 0.007), and both duplicate the θ=0 facts under several names. Neither includes the gain-correction law GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK) or the previous-time-step implementation detail.
remarks: Figure 7-4's x-axis only spans roughly 0-23°, so every claim conditioned on 25° (three in each set) is unsupported; both sets treat the plot as if it extended to 25°. Both sets also re-derive the θ=0 gains from the curve (0.020 s, 0.007, 0.008, 0.0081) even though the text gives them exactly, producing conflicting duplicates. Quotes in both sets are mostly axis/legend labels that do not support the numeric values, and Set B additionally embeds values (e.g. "... 0.002 ...") that appear nowhere in the source text. Facts both sets miss: Eq. (7-20) GK(θ)=1/(1+θ/θK), the use of the previous time step's blade-pitch angle to compute GK for the next step, and the stated limitation that the simple gain-scheduling law cannot keep ωφn and ζφ constant.
